question: An 18-month-old with acute watery diarrhoea and 'some dehydration' is being managed with ORT. The mother asks why plain water is not sufficient and why a special solution is needed. Which ONE statement BEST explains the physiological rationale for ORS?

answers.text: ORS works by inhibiting intestinal secretion of chloride ions through blockade of cAMP pathways activated by toxins.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. ORS does not inhibit toxin-driven secretion. Cholera toxin (and rotavirus NSP4) continues to drive chloride secretion even in the presence of ORS. ORS works by an entirely separate mechanism — glucose-coupled sodium absorption.

answers.text: ORS replaces water and electrolytes via glucose-coupled sodium co-transport (SGLT1), which remains intact even when toxin-driven secretion is active.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. SGLT1 (sodium-glucose co-transporter) on the brush border of enterocytes absorbs sodium and glucose together at a 1:1 molar ratio, dragging water by osmosis. This absorptive pathway is independent of, and not impaired by, cAMP-mediated secretory pathways activated by cholera toxin or rotavirus. The WHO reduced-osmolarity ORS (245 mOsm/L) contains: Na 75 mEq, Cl 65 mEq, K 20 mEq, citrate 10 mEq, glucose 75 mmol.

answers.text: Plain water is unsafe because it worsens hyperkalaemia by driving water into cells and shifting potassium out.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The main risk of plain water in severe diarrhoea is hyponatraemia (dilutional), not hyperkalaemia. Plain water lacks the electrolytes and glucose needed to drive active sodium absorption via SGLT1.

answers.text: ORS is superior because it contains antibiotics that reduce the duration of diarrhoea.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. ORS contains no antibiotics. Its superiority is purely based on the glucose-coupled sodium absorption principle. Antibiotics are NOT routinely recommended in acute watery diarrhoea; they are reserved for specific invasive pathogens (e.g. Shigella, Vibrio cholerae) or immunocompromised hosts.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key principle: cholera toxin inhibits Na/Cl absorption via cAMP, but CANNOT inhibit glucose-coupled sodium absorption (SGLT1). ORS gives glucose + sodium → SGLT1 absorption is preserved. WHO reduced-osmolarity ORS: Na 75, glucose 75 mmol, osmolarity 245 mOsm/L.

Correct. ORS exploits glucose-coupled sodium absorption (SGLT1), which is preserved during secretory diarrhoea. The WHO reduced-osmolarity ORS (245 mOsm/L) is the standard. Zinc supplementation (10–20 mg/day for 10–14 days) reduces severity and prevents recurrence.
